headline: Sales edge up on the Simple Mills deal, but profit slips
summary_short: Net sales rose 1.1% y/y to $1,571.6M (16-week Q1 ended April 25, 2026) as the Simple Mills acquisition and pricing/mix offset a 3.3% volume decline, while net income fell 20.6% y/y to $42.1M and diluted EPS dropped $0.05 to $0.20.
summary_long: Net sales grew 1.1% y/y to $1,571.6M: pricing/mix +2.1%, the Simple Mills acquisition +2.3%, volume -3.3%. Net income fell 20.6% y/y to $42.1M on a challenging consumer environment and $5.6M higher net interest expense from Simple Mills-related debt, partly offset by the absence of prior-year plant closure costs and moderating ingredient costs. Adjusted EBITDA was $159.0M, down 1.8% y/y (margin -30bp to 10.1%). The board declared a $0.1250/share quarterly dividend (reset from the prior rate as part of an ongoing capital-strategy review), the 95th consecutive quarterly payout. Cash and equivalents were $11.5M at quarter end vs $12.1M at fiscal year-end. Management reaffirmed full-year FY2026 guidance.

drivers.explanation: Simple Mills acquisition (+2.3%) and pricing/mix (+2.1%) more than offset a 3.3% volume decline amid a challenging consumer environment.
Challenging consumer environment and $5.6M higher net interest expense from Simple Mills acquisition debt, partly offset by absence of prior-year plant closure costs and moderating ingredient costs.
Materials/labor/production costs rose 50bp to 50.6% of sales on higher outside-purchase mix and lower production volumes, offsetting moderating ingredient costs — kept gross margin roughly flat y/y.
SD&A expenses rose 10bp to 40.9% of sales on higher workforce costs and greater legal-settlement and restructuring-implementation costs, partly offset by lower distributor distribution fees.
